exposure: Women with self-measured blood glucose levels and routine obstetric examination
Women with non-self-measured blood glucose levels and double obstetric examination
Subgroups based on self-management modes (dietary diary, treadmill use)
cohort: 835 women with GDM at the Second Hospital of Tianjin Medical University, Tianjin, China from January 1, 2016 to December 31, 2018
finding: Self-monitoring of blood glucose levels plus a routine obstetric examination in women with GDM was associated with better blood sugar control, lower cesarean section rates, and lower prevalence of LGA and macrosomia compared to non-self-monitoring and double obstetric examinations.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate was significantly lower in the self-monitoring group compared to the non-self-monitoring group.
birth_weight: Birth weight was significantly lower in the self-monitoring group compared to the non-self-monitoring group
